Dear Marie Cooksey

The following Task has been in a status of Logged with HRIS Management Team since 09/06/2026 10:53:41 (UTC) - Etc/UTC:

Task: 50959264
Summary: IAM request for access to HR data from Core User Directory for Groupstore

Open:Task <https://oxford.saasiteu.com/Login.aspx?Scope=ObjectWorkspace&CommandId=Search&ObjectType=Task%23Assignment&CommandData=AssignmentId,%3D,0,50959264,1,AND>

Task Details:

Dear HRIS Management Team,

 

In order to resolve OSM Problem P#40000852, the Identity and Access Management Team (IAM) are adding additional Groupstore groups for each department to distinguish types of HRIS staff (casual and non-casual) from people with University Staff cards.  This requires access to the following two attributes from Core User Directory (CUD) for all employees:

 

New attributes required:

cud:uas_hris:primary_post_department_code

cud:uas_hris:primary_post_appointment_id

 

The reason for access is:

"These two attributes will be used to determine casual vs. non-casual staff within Groupstore, allowing us to publish groups of users for access control purposes.

Currently, people are classed as University Staff if they have a Card with US status or have a live HRIS affiliation for the department. Unfortunately for some departments, it is necessary to distinguish between casual staff and normal staff as casual staff may well be students working over the summer. Groupstore needs to check if the post's primary department matches the current department being processed, hence primary_post_department_code."

 

A previous request covered the use of these attributes in a test environment.  However, this request is for use of live HRIS data in the production environment.

 

As data custodians for HRIS, do you approve of this use case and the release of attributes for this purpose?

Subject: Patch Release 28.0.157 – UAT Update

 

Morning,

Patch Release 28.0.157 – UAT Update

Due to annual leave and other commitments, I reviewed the latest 28.0.157 patch release notes myself. I just wanted to share a few updates for info ahead of the release, which is due to go into Production next week.

Absence Reason Filter

People Management > Employee Search > Absences > Add Absence > Tab 2 – More

A recent change made by Access Group switched the Absence Reason field to paged mode but did not carry over the search-as-you-type setting. As a result, any text entered into the field was ignored, meaning users had to scroll through the full list of absence reasons.  I’m not aware of any users actually querying this though.  

Access Group have now reinstated the search-as-you-type functionality.

During testing, I found that the search now narrows the list as you type, but it appears to work consistently only when searching on the first word within an absence reason. Searching using part of a subsequent word was not always consistent.

I've fed this back to Access Group as part of our testing.

________________________________

NI Number Column Added to Employee Search

People Management > Employee Search

A new NI Number column has been added to the Employee Search screen, positioned to the right of the Personnel No. column.

While testing in UAT, I noticed that the new column does not have a column heading. I raised this with Access Group, who confirmed that, after checking with Development, this is the intended design.

I've responded to say that this seems an unusual design decision, as every other column on the screen has a header. From a usability perspective, a column heading would make the interface clearer and more consistent. I've asked that this feedback is passed to the Development team for consideration in a future release.

________________________________

Staff Request Rejection Notifications

Additional data merge fields have been made available for staff request notification emails, including:

*	Name of the person rejecting the request.
*	Rejection reason.

I still need to test these, but this looks promising as it should allow us to include more meaningful information in staff request rejection notifications.  If testing proves successful I will raise a change for approval to update the rejection notifications.

Just also with the above, some choices made by yourselves will dictate what we would need to cover, so for example, we need to decide with the Company, do we want to copy a preexisting Company or create from scratch. Similarly, we also need to decide the same for Pay Group. 

 

For the Pay Groups, on UOXU for example, there is Pay Groups 99(Non Employees) and 2221(Test PG), if these were suitable, we can use one of these as the template to create our new non payroll pay group so that we can link this to the new Organisation. If not, we can of course create from scratch.

 


1. Payroll Company – Create New vs Copy


Copy Existing Company (Recommended)


When to use:

*	New company is similar to an existing one
*	Same country, payroll rules, or configuration structure

Benefits:

*	Faster setup – most fields pre-populated
*	Reduces risk of missing key payroll parameters
*	Ensures consistency across companies

What to review after copying:

*	Company Code and Name
*	Contact and registration details
*	Currency, payroll provider, and bank details
*	Payroll parameters (e.g. pay codes, cost centres) 

Key consideration:
Copying is best practice as it “cuts down processing time” and only requires minor updates rather than full configuration 

________________________________


Create New Company (From Scratch)


When to use:

*	Company has different payroll requirements
*	Different country, legislation, or setup
*	No suitable template exists

Considerations:

*	All fields must be manually configured
*	Higher risk of missing mandatory payroll settings
*	More time-consuming

Key takeaway:
Use only when structure or payroll rules differ significantly from existing companies.

With the Pay Group it is as below:

 


2. Pay Group – Create New vs Copy


Copy / Duplicate Pay Group (Recommended)


When to use:

*	New pay group follows same structure (even if non-payroll)
*	Same pay frequency or similar setup

Benefits:

*	Saves time vs building from scratch
*	Retains correct configuration (periods, indicators, thresholds)
*	Reduces configuration errors

What to update:

*	Pay Group Code and Description
*	Pay frequency (if different)
*	Key indicators (e.g. timesheet, salary settings) 

Key consideration:
Duplication is specifically designed to “save time when configuring multiple new pay groups” 

________________________________


Create New Pay Group (From Scratch)


When to use:

*	Unique pay setup required (e.g. different frequency or behaviour)
*	No existing template matches requirements

Considerations:

*	Must define all mandatory fields (periods, frequency, indicators)
*	Requires correct linkage to company
*	More manual effort and validation

1. Payroll Company – Create New vs Copy


Copy Existing Company (Recommended)


When to use:

*	New company is similar to an existing one
*	Same country, payroll rules, or configuration structure

Benefits:

*	Faster setup – most fields pre-populated
*	Reduces risk of missing key payroll parameters
*	Ensures consistency across companies

What to review after copying:

*	Company Code and Name
*	Contact and registration details
*	Currency, payroll provider, and bank details
*	Payroll parameters (e.g. pay codes, cost centres) 

Key consideration:
Copying is best practice as it “cuts down processing time” and only requires minor updates rather than full configuration 

________________________________


Create New Company (From Scratch)


When to use:

*	Company has different payroll requirements
*	Different country, legislation, or setup
*	No suitable template exists

Considerations:

*	All fields must be manually configured
*	Higher risk of missing mandatory payroll settings
*	More time-consuming

Key takeaway:
Use only when structure or payroll rules differ significantly from existing companies.

With the Pay Group it is as below:

 


2. Pay Group – Create New vs Copy


Copy / Duplicate Pay Group (Recommended)


When to use:

*	New pay group follows same structure (even if non-payroll)
*	Same pay frequency or similar setup

Benefits:

*	Saves time vs building from scratch
*	Retains correct configuration (periods, indicators, thresholds)
*	Reduces configuration errors

What to update:

*	Pay Group Code and Description
*	Pay frequency (if different)
*	Key indicators (e.g. timesheet, salary settings) 

Key consideration:
Duplication is specifically designed to “save time when configuring multiple new pay groups” 

________________________________


Create New Pay Group (From Scratch)


When to use:

*	Unique pay setup required (e.g. different frequency or behaviour)
*	No existing template matches requirements

Considerations:

*	Must define all mandatory fields (periods, frequency, indicators)
*	Requires correct linkage to company
*	More manual effort and validation

entries.subject: Business rules for Data Warehouse
entries.body:
Hi Ewan,

 

In our meeting this morning we agreed that I would confirm the rules that would need to be put in place to ensure that only University data is being processed in the current data warehouse and the future Fabric solution. Separately we will tackle the best way of getting Company 90 data into a separate area of the warehouse.

 

It was proposed that we would likely need to pull all of the data into the data warehouse and then use logic within the bronze layer to ensure we’re only surfacing and processing further data from within the University domain. The logic for how we can approach this is as follows:

 

Employee & Appointment Related Tables

In order to ensure only University data in passed into our data warehouse solution we need to restrict appointment level data to any appointment IDs which meet the following rules:

*	Company = 10 
*	The sum of days a company 10 appointment held, by person_reference > 1

 

We can then use this group of employees and appointments to restrict other tables which aren’t directly linked to appointment data (for example, person level information, UDF information, etc).

 

Examples of tables which will need to link appointment_id to the logic table in order to filter on company 10 appointments only:

[PEOPLEHR].[CT_BALANCE_ADJUSTMENT]

[PEOPLEHR].[CTBI_PERSON_CALCULATED_HOURS]

[PEOPLEHR].[PABI_PERSON_PENSION_SCHEME]

[PEOPLEHR].[PRBI_PERSON_USER_DATA_ATITL]

[PEOPLEHR].[PRBI_PERSON_COST_ALLOCATIONS]

 

For employee level information we will need to again link back to this logic table to check which employee records count as University records (we must not use “Company” to filter on any of these tables, even if it exists due to the way that data can be processed within PeopleXD causing errors).

 

Examples of tables which don’t contain appointment ID but do contain Person Reference, so we will need to link person_reference back to the logic table:

[PEOPLEHR].[ONBOARDING_PERS_COMPLETE_ITEMS]

[PEOPLEHR].[PABI_PERSON_MASTER]

[PEOPLEHR].[PRBI_HR_PERSON_MASTER]

[PEOPLEHR].[PRBI_PERSON_CONTACT]

[PEOPLEHR].[PRBI_PERSON_QUALIFICATIONS]

 

Payroll Related Tables

Within Payroll tables we can use the Pay Group to restrict to the main University. Where Pay Group is available within the payroll tables we can restrict on Pay Groups 20, 21 and 99. 

 

Examples of tables which rely on Pay Group to filter on pay group 20, 21 and 99 only:

[PEOPLEHR].[PABI_PAY_HISTORY]

[PEOPLEHR].[PABI_PAY_HISTORY_CAS]

[PEOPLEHR].[PAY_GROUP]

 

Recruitment and post appointment data

Where data is related to post management we can safely utilise the Company Code held against these records to filter without any complex logic being required. We also don’t expect any recruitment data outside of company 10 to exist in the system so this is a low risk area.

 

Examples of tables where using Company Code to filter Company = 10 only:

[PEOPLEHR].[RTBI_STAFF_REQUESTS]

[PEOPLEHR].[RTBI_COMPETITION_MASTER]

 

Reference / Other Data

 

There’s also a number of tables which are loaded with reference data or externally derived data which won’t need any filtering, some of which we may wish to replicate in whatever the college data area looks like, and some we definitely won’t want to replicate.

Examples of tables which are reference data or not related to individuals or specific companies which won’t need any filtering (some of which may need duplicating in whatever the college area looks like):

[PEOPLEHR].[CTBI_BALANCE_HOLIDAY_SCHEME_MAPPING]

[PEOPLEHR].[EARNING_LIMITS]

[PEOPLEHR].[EXT_LOAD_UCEA_BROAD_SICKNESS_ABSENCE_REASONS]

[PEOPLEHR].[HR_HIERARCHY_DATA_VIEW]

[PEOPLEHR].[PEBI_PENSION_SCHEME_DETAILS]

[PEOPLEHR].[PRBI_APPOINTMENT_REASON_LOV]

 

Examples of external load files which won’t need any filtering and definitely won’t need to exist in the college area:

[PEOPLEHR].[EXT_LOAD_HEIDI_PLUS_ALL_CURRENT_USERS]

 

@Ewan Kilgour <mailto:ewan.kilgour@it.ox.ac.uk>  I think we will probably need to work through all of the tables which are populated in Bronze and establish how / if we need to restrict to Company 10. Do you agree? Or is the above enough for your team to come up with a proposal?

 

Many thanks,

Simon

Hi Sarah,

 

Following our conversations in the office yesterday regarding the HESA LEVEL and SOC UDFs, I thought it would be helpful to follow up on this email chain used when escalating the case with AG, so that Simon/Kevin are also updated at the same time.  

 

Background to bring everyone up to speed:

AG successfully ran the script against one test employee record from our list. We then agreed for the full bulk script to be run in UOXU, which AG completed on Tuesday evening.

 

When reviewing the Insight report that Sarah created, the deleted records were not returned, which aligns with what AG expected. However, when Sarah ran the same dataset through Alteryx, the records that should have been deleted were still appearing.

 

I went back to AG to query this, but they remain confident that the data has been deleted, as the same script was used and Insight is no longer returning the records. This makes the situation a little awkward, as Insight does appear to support their position.

 

It has been suggested that Alteryx may be returning cached data, as it is known to cache inputs silently. To rule this out, could we try clearing all Alteryx caches and re‑running the workflow using a fresh link to the latest Insight return?

 

The recommended steps are:

•             Right‑click the Input tool → Clear Cache

•             Disable any Cache and Run settings

•             Check whether any temporary yxdb files are being referenced

•             Re‑run the workflow from scratch with caching disabled, ensuring it is pointing to the latest Insight data.

 

 

This may help us confirm whether the discrepancy is due to cached data rather than an issue with the deletion itself.

 

 

Best wishes,

Michael
